page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance running under the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a nominal clock speed of 2.7 GHz, delivering 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores across 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Vector acceleration is supported via instruction extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware cryptography instructions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes 48 MB of L3 cache, provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps, and contains no local storage or discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate mixed performance across varying workload types. In stress-ng, single-core CPU throughput reached 1858.18 (average), whereas multi-core throughput registered 3853.92 (weak), reflecting the limited physical core count of a 2-core footprint. PassMark testing mirrored this trend, reporting an overall CPU score of 5887.68 (weak) alongside an encryption test result of 3618.05 (average). Single-threaded tasks exhibited stable results, achieving 27.56 GB/sec in gzip compression and 10.67 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, though multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scored 20.89 GB/sec (poor). Memory metrics demonstrated 25.91 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB write tests and an overall PassMark memory score of 2387.77 (average), while large block uncached read bandwidth remained at 30.29 GB/sec.

Network and application layer benchmarks indicate balanced throughput for memory-bound, moderate compute tasks. The instance delivered a static web serving throughput of 6.41 GB/sec and sustained 3.99 million Redis SET operations per second. In lightweight artificial intelligence inferencing with a 135M parameter model, prompt processing achieved 406.27 tokens per second, with text generation reaching 103.36 tokens per second. Because the server lacks local ephemeral NVMe disks and bundled public IPv4 addresses, storage must be managed entirely over network-attached block devices.

The ecs.r7.xlarge profile provides high memory density relative to core count, making it well-suited for medium-scale in-memory caching layers, Redis instances, small relational databases, and enterprise applications that require significant memory footprints without high parallel compute demands.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8369B cores at 2.7 GHz and 32.0 GB of RAM, offering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Built on x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it includes 48 MB of L3 cache, 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and supports AVX-512 instruction sets. It lacks bundled local storage and discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate balanced single-threaded processing (27.56 GB/sec in gzip compression) and steady memory write speeds (25.91 GB/sec uncached), though multi-core throughput remains restricted by the two-core allocation. Application performance includes 3.99 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.41 GB/sec static web throughput. This server is best suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, and lightweight backend services requiring dedicated memory headroom.
